traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Guttiferae, which takes in Calophyllaceae: leaves usually opposite, sometimes alternate or whorled; leaves simple; margins entire; veins pinnate; stipules present or absent; plants hermaphrodite, monoecious, polygamous or dioecious; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems woody or herbaceous; flowers in cymes, in umbels or in panicles, rarely solitary; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals or spiral; fruit capsule, berry or drupe; stamens (3-) 5 to 100; carpels (1-) 3 to 5 (-13). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: DELTA Guttiferae (read 2026-10-16): mostly opposite (Caraipa, Kielmeyera alternate).

traits.fruit_type.note: DELTA Guttiferae s.l. (read 2026-10-17): capsule, berry or drupe, unweighted. Wikipedia (read 2026-10-17): Calophyllaceae ~475 spp in ~14 genera; Calophyllum alone has 204 spp (over 40%) with a thin-fleshed drupe. Other genera (Mammea, Kielmeyera, Mesua, Caraipa) not read; capsular Kielmeyera and Caraipa together are far smaller than Calophyllum.

traits.inflorescence.note: DELTA Guttiferae s.l. (read 2026-10-17): terminal cymose groups, often umbel-like or paniculate. Wikipedia Calophyllum (read 2026-10-17; 204 of ~475 family spp): axillary or terminal cymes or thyrses. Thyrse kept as panicle.

traits.perianth.note: DELTA Guttiferae s.l. (read 2026-10-17): calyx and corolla distinct or intergrading. Wikipedia Calophyllum (read 2026-10-17; over 40% of family species): sepals and petals in whorls, sometimes alike.
